template: Make eye contact, smile, and say hello to 10 different strangers during one outing.
Give a specific, respectful compliment about style or vibe to 5 strangers and then walk away without lingering.
Start a short conversation with someone you find attractive in a public place, keep it under 2 minutes, and exit gracefully.
Ask someone you find attractive for a genuine recommendation such as a coffee, food, or local spot and sincerely thank them.
Chat with the person in front of or behind you in a line until the line moves and your transaction is done.
At a bar, café, or event, introduce yourself by name to someone you find attractive and ask their name too.
Ask someone what they’re drinking or eating, say you were curious about it, and react with a real comment.
Start a conversation about something happening around you such as the music, crowd, or venue and keep it going for at least 60 seconds.
Ask someone how their night is going and follow up with at least one curious question based on their answer.
Give one compliment that includes why you like that thing such as “That jacket is fire, the color really fits you.” then exit politely.
Ask someone you find attractive for directions or help finding something and add one extra sentence of small talk before leaving.
Join a small group conversation where you know no one and contribute at least two comments before excusing yourself.
Ask someone you find attractive what brings them here tonight and ask one follow-up question about their answer.
Make one light-hearted, non-insulting joke with someone new and stay present for their reaction without nervously backtracking.
Ask someone to help you choose between two items, follow their suggestion, and briefly chat about why they picked it.
Hold a conversation with a stranger for at least 3 minutes without checking your phone once.
Ask someone if they live in the area or are visiting, then ask what they like most about where they’re from.
Ask a stranger what their favorite thing about this city is and share your own favorite after they answer.
Approach a small group and ask a fun opinion question such as “We’re deciding: X or Y, what do you think?” then thank them and bounce.
Tell someone you just wanted to say hi because they seemed interesting or had good energy, then introduce yourself.
Ask someone what they like to do for fun outside of work or school and ask one follow-up question based on their answer.
Stand or sit in a social spot for 10 minutes with open body language and no phone, letting people see you are approachable.
Ask someone about what they’re reading, wearing, or working on and let them talk for at least 30 seconds before you reply.
Give one compliment that is not about looks but about vibe or behavior such as “You seem like you’re having a fun night, I like that.”
Ask someone what they’re celebrating or what the occasion is for their night out if it feels appropriate and natural.
Ask if a seat near someone is taken, sit down, and have at least 90 seconds of conversation before leaving.
Ask someone to take a photo of you or your group, then thank them and add one extra line of small talk before parting.
Give a respectful compliment to someone in a group and then walk away without lingering or hovering around them.
Ask someone for a bar, restaurant, or café recommendation, then ask if they’ve been anywhere similar recently.
During a conversation with someone you find attractive, hold comfortable eye contact for at least 10 seconds at a time while you talk.
Ask someone what kind of music they like and follow up with a question about artists, concerts, or playlists.
Approach someone who is also alone at an event and ask how they heard about it, then share how you found it.
Ask someone what a perfect off-day looks like for them, then share what a perfect day off looks like for you.
Give a compliment and stay present if they compliment you back instead of deflecting or talking yourself down.
Ask where they got a specific item they’re wearing, respond with real interest, and then let the conversation end naturally.
In one night out, intentionally start conversations with at least 3 different people or groups you didn’t know.
Ask someone if they are originally from this city and ask what they like or don’t like about living here.
On purpose, collect 3 gentle rejections in one night by respectfully approaching people and accepting any no with a smile.
Ask someone what they do for fun outside of work and let them talk for at least 45 seconds without interrupting.
Ask a stranger or group if they know another good spot nearby and consider actually going to their suggestion.
In a conversation with someone you’re attracted to, consciously slow down your speech instead of rushing or rambling.
Ask someone what their go-to comfort food or show is and share yours after they answer.
Walk up to someone and say, “You seemed cool, I wanted to say hi,” then introduce yourself and ask their name.
Compliment someone’s style, then ask how they would describe their style or where they like to shop.
Join a dance floor or high-energy area for at least one whole song even if you feel awkward and self-conscious.
Ask someone to recommend a song or artist, then later that night actually listen to at least one track from them.
Stand in the most social area of the room for 10 minutes without touching your phone, just taking in the space.
Ask someone how they know the host or found this event, then share your connection or reason for being there.
Take a conversation from surface-level topics into something slightly deeper such as goals, dreams, or favorite memories.
Ask someone what the highlight of their week has been so far and share your highlight after they answer.
In one outing, give 3 compliments: one about style, one about energy, and one about something they’re doing.
Ask someone for their social media or phone number in a clear, respectful way and accept any answer without asking twice.
After at least a 5-minute conversation, ask if they’d be open to grabbing coffee or a drink another time, clearly but casually.
Get at least one contact from someone you’re genuinely attracted to during a night out, even if it takes multiple tries.
Ask someone you’re attracted to on a clear, respectful date such as coffee or a casual drink and accept their answer without pressure.
On a dating app, send 10 first messages that are personal and specific instead of copy-paste openers.
Take one active chat from a dating app or social media and propose a specific plan with a day range and type of date.
Ask someone you find attractive a playful, low-stakes question such as “pizza or tacos?” and riff with their answer for at least 30 seconds.
In one outing, approach 5 people who are standing or sitting alone and make small talk for at least 30 seconds each.
Ask someone what their favorite type of night out is such as quiet bar, loud club, or house hang and share your own answer.
Give a compliment to someone who intimidates you a little and then walk away without downplaying yourself internally.
At a bar or café, ask someone what they’re working on or reading and respond with one thoughtful comment.
Approach someone with headphones in, politely gesture, and ask if they have a minute to answer a fun question. If they say no, thank them and move on.
Ask someone what they’re celebrating if they’re clearly in a fun group mood, then wish them a genuinely good night.
Collect 5 small brush-offs or quick no’s in one week of going out and log each one without judging yourself.
Ask someone what kind of trips or travel they like doing, then share one place you’d like to visit someday.
Ask a stranger for a genuine style opinion such as “Which of these looks better on me?” and accept whatever they say with a smile.
Approach someone in a chill area and ask if they mind you joining the table or standing nearby, then chat briefly if they say yes.
Ask someone what their dream job or dream lifestyle looks like and share a piece of yours afterward.
Have a full conversation with someone you find attractive while standing tall, shoulders back, instead of shrinking yourself.
Ask someone new what their favorite local spot is for food or drinks and write it down or save it in your phone after.
Approach someone and say you’re practicing talking to more people and ask if you can ask them a fun question. Accept any no calmly.
Ask someone what their favorite type of music to dance to is and if you’re in a dance setting, stay for one song of that genre if it comes on.
Collect one clear yes or no to a date or hangout invitation in a week, instead of keeping things in endless flirting limbo.
Ask someone if they want to join you for a quick game such as pool, darts, or a bar game and play one round if they agree.
Approach a pair of people and ask a simple, fun group question, letting both respond before you leave.
Have a 5-minute conversation with someone you’re attracted to where you talk as much about them as you do about yourself.
Collect 10 short small-talk reps in one night whether at bars, cafés, lines, or events without trying to turn all of them into flirting.
Ask someone what they’re into outside of work and follow up by asking how they got into it in the first place.
Go out one night with the specific goal of collecting at least 2 rejections and 2 neutral or positive interactions, tracking each one mentally.
Ask someone what their favorite way to spend a Sunday is and share yours, then exit the conversation before it dies on its own.
Approach someone and ask which song they would pick if they could control the vibe right now, then talk about it briefly.
Take one night to practice only opening lines and quick chats without asking for any contact info at all.
Ask someone what kind of people they vibe with best and share one quality you like in people you’re drawn to.
In a conversation, admit one small non-heavy truth about yourself such as being new to the city or trying to talk to more people.
Ask someone what they’d rather do: stay in with movies or go out dancing, then share your preference and one short story behind it.
Approach 3 people or groups who look welcoming, even if you’re nervous, and say at least one full sentence to each before deciding if you’ll stay or leave.
Ask someone what their favorite kind of night in looks like and share one detail about yours that shows your personality.
End a conversation on purpose while it’s still going well by saying you enjoyed talking and wishing them a good night, instead of waiting for awkward silence.
Ask someone where they would take a friend visiting from out of town, then share where you would take someone visiting you.
Spend one night out wearing something you actually feel confident in and consciously open at least 5 interactions while wearing it.
Approach someone you find attractive and ask, “Honest opinion—should I order X or Y?” and then follow their choice.
Ask someone what they do but then immediately follow up by asking what they’d do if money and time weren’t a problem.
In one week, attempt at least 3 clear invitations such as coffee, walk, or drink and write down how each one went afterward.
Ask someone for their number or social handle, and if they hesitate or say no, respond with genuine “All good, nice meeting you.” and mean it.
Have one night where your only metric of success is number of conversations started, not numbers or dates gained. Aim for at least 8 openings.
Ask someone what they think makes a good conversation with a stranger and listen to their full answer without interrupting.
When you feel intimidated by someone’s looks or presence, walk directly past them once with your posture tall, then later give one small compliment if the moment feels right.
Take one person from a short, fun interaction to exchanging contact info within the same outing, even if your voice shakes a little.
In one week, collect at least 5 rejections or brush-offs and 5 neutral or positive responses, proving to yourself that both can coexist and you are still fine.
